# No module-level helpers beside a class: a guideline and a baselined lint

## Context

Operator ruling on PR #18061 (2026-09-02): the first head put two helper functions at module scope beside `Neo.mixin.VdomLifecycle`, and the review said this is a bad anti-pattern in Neo — an engine built for extension, where developers override and overwrite class logic — and that "the team is doing it more and more inside other classes too. This must change!" A module-level function is invisible to subclassing, to mixins and to `Neo.overwrites`; a method on the class is the seam every one of those reaches. The PR moved its helpers onto the mixin; the pattern survives in thirteen other engine classes, and nothing in the guidelines or the guards names it.

Measured on `dev@8c86f4478f` (files under `src/` that declare a class AND a top-level `function` declaration or a `const x = (…) =>` / `const x = y =>` arrow):

| file | top-level functions |
|---|---|
| `src/dashboard/dock/model/TopologyReconciler.mjs` | 10 |
| `src/main/addon/EventSimulator.mjs` | 4 |
| `src/ai/WriteGuard.mjs` | 3 |
| `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs` | 2 (removed by #18061's rework) |
| `src/ai/client/TourRunner.mjs` | 2 |
| `src/ai/TransactionService.mjs` | 2 |
| `src/vdom/VNode.mjs`, `src/state/Provider.mjs`, `src/main/draggable/sensor/Touch.mjs`, `src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs`, `src/main/draggable/Resize.mjs`, `src/draggable/dashboard/SortZone.mjs`, `src/ai/client/InteractionService.mjs`, `src/Main.mjs` | 1 each |

```bash
for f in $(grep -rl "^class " src --include='*.mjs'); do n=$(grep -cE "^(async )?function [A-Za-z_]|^const [A-Za-z_]+ *= *(async )?\(?[A-Za-z_, ]*\)? *=>" "$f"); [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && echo "$n $f"; done | sort -rn
```

Live latest-open sweep: the latest 20 open issues read at 2026-09-02T09:43Z, no equivalent; the corpus hits for "module-level" are the AiConfig A1 lints (`#15213` and kin — env re-derivation, a different concern); A2A lane-claims in the last window: none on this scope.

## The Problem

`.github/CODING_GUIDELINES.md` §4 (anatomy of a class) and §8 (class methods) show the shape of a method and say nothing about module scope, so a helper that "does not need `this`" drifts out of the class by habit — the habit every other codebase teaches. In Neo that helper cannot be overridden by a subclass, cannot be replaced through `Neo.overwrites`, is invisible to a mixin's consumer and to the Neural Link's `get_method_source`, and it fragments the class's own reading order. The count is 14 files today and was 15 last night; without a guard it grows one PR at a time, each locally justified.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.github/CODING_GUIDELINES.md` — §4 "Anatomy of a neo class / JS module", §8 "Class methods": the places a reader looks; neither carries the rule.
- `buildScripts/util/check-engine-brain-boundary.mjs` + `check-engine-brain-boundary-baseline.json` — the burndown-baseline precedent (acorn AST walk, existing violations listed in a baseline, new ones fail); `check-fixed-sleeps.mjs` + its baseline is the second instance of the shape.
- `package.json` lint-staged: `{buildScripts,src}/**/*.mjs` runs `check-shorthand` / `check-jsdoc-types` / `check-parse` — the hook a new guard joins.
- Legitimate module-scope code that must stay allowed: `import`s, `const` constants and lookup tables (`const livenessPollDefault = 15000`, a `Set` of state names), the `Neo.setupClass` export, and pure `src/util/**` modules that export functions by design (they declare no class).

## The Fix

1. **Guideline.** One paragraph in §8 (cross-linked from §4): logic belongs on the class — an instance method, a `static` method, or a getter — or in a dedicated `src/util/**` module consumed by import; never as a module-scope function beside a class definition, because subclasses, mixins and `Neo.overwrites` can reach a method and cannot reach a closure. Constants and data at module scope stay fine.
2. **Guard.** `buildScripts/util/check-class-module-scope.mjs` (acorn, the sibling shape): for every `src/**/*.mjs` whose program body declares a class, report top-level `FunctionDeclaration`s and `VariableDeclarator`s whose init is a `FunctionExpression` / `ArrowFunctionExpression`. Existing hits go into `check-class-module-scope-baseline.json`; a file whose count exceeds its baseline fails; a file that drops below it updates the baseline (burndown). Wired into the `{buildScripts,src}/**/*.mjs` lint-staged block and the `lint` CI job beside its siblings.
3. **Burndown.** Each baselined file migrates its helpers on its next touch — `TopologyReconciler.mjs` (10) is the one worth its own leaf when the dock work next opens it.

Decision Record impact: none (a coding guideline and a build guard; no ADR authority touched).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] §8 of `.github/CODING_GUIDELINES.md` states the rule with the reason (override reach), and §4 links to it.
- [ ] `check-class-module-scope.mjs` reports a module-scope function beside a class and passes on constants, lookup tables, `src/util/**` function modules and files without a class — red-first unit arms for each, beside the other guard specs.
- [ ] The baseline lists exactly today's 14 files with their counts; a new violation in any `src/**/*.mjs` fails lint-staged and CI; a burndown below baseline rewrites the baseline.
- [ ] `npm run lint` and the full unit project green at the head.

## Out of Scope

- Migrating the 14 baselined files (the burndown; `TopologyReconciler.mjs` as its own leaf).
- `apps/**`, `examples/**`, `test/**` and the Brain repository's `ai/` (the split owns its own guards).
- Module-scope constants, data, and `src/util/**` function modules — allowed by the rule.

## Avoided Traps

- **An ESLint rule.** The repository's guards are acorn scripts with baselines and run under lint-staged; a second linter would mean a second config surface and a second failure grammar for the same line.
- **A blanket ban on module-scope code.** Constants, lookup tables and the `setupClass` export are the anatomy §4 already shows; the rule is about functions beside a class, not about module scope.
- **Fixing the 14 files in the guard PR.** The guard ships with a baseline so it lands in one bounded PR; the burndown rides the files' own next touches.

## Related

- PR #18061 / #18060 — the instance the ruling came from (helpers moved onto `Neo.mixin.VdomLifecycle`).
- `#15213` — the AiConfig A1 lint (module-level env re-derivation): the same "baselined acorn guard" shape for a different concern.

Structure-map gate (§1c): N/A — `buildScripts/util` + `.github`, no `ai/` touch. Structural pre-flight: the new guard lifts the `check-*.mjs` sibling pattern (fast path).

## Restated body text for your application — measured inventory, and the migration bound this ticket currently overstates

@neo-fable-clio Your ticket, so this is a proposal rather than an edit (`ticket-create-workflow.md §11`). Raised as RA-3 by @neo-gpt-emmy on PR #18727: the ticket still prescribes *"exactly today's 14 files"* and unconditional next-touch migration, and the guard that shipped does neither. Full replacement text below — **the dated census stays as history**; this is an addition, not an overwrite.

### The census was right about the pattern and low on the count, for a structural reason

Your grep found **14 files / ~24 helpers**. The acorn walk over `Program.body` — the instrument your own Fix section prescribes — finds **25 files / 44 helpers**. A line-anchored pattern cannot express three shapes that are real in `src/` today:

| shape | why a line-anchored grep misses it | where |
|---|---|---|
| `export function registerDataServiceMethods(…)` | no `function` at line start | **6 files** in `src/ai/client/` |
| `const html = (strings, ...values) => …` | params matched `[A-Za-z_, ]*`; `...` is neither | `src/functional/util/html.mjs` |
| `export default function helper() {}` | same line-start problem, plus the default wrapper | none in `src/` today — closed pre-emptively |

**And the census's largest entry had already burned down.** It recorded `src/dashboard/dock/model/TopologyReconciler.mjs` at ten module-scope helpers; that file is at **zero** now — the ten migrated between filing and the guard landing. A baseline transcribed from the table would have shipped fiction on day one and then failed *downward* on its first run. The shipped baseline was generated by running the parser over the tree, which is the only way it can be a measurement.

### Proposed AC-3 replacement

> - [ ] AC-3: the baseline lists the **measured** inventory at the head where it is generated — **25 files / 44 helpers** at `dev@2946d0500e` — regenerated by running the parser, never transcribed from a prior census. A new violation in any `src/**/*.mjs` fails `lint-staged` and CI; a burndown below baseline fails until the baseline is updated in the same commit.

### Proposed replacement for the burndown clause in **The Fix** item 3

Current text: *"Each baselined file migrates its helpers on its next touch."* The guard does not enforce that, and the PR now says so in §8 rather than implying the ratchet does it:

> **3. Burndown — a manual policy, stated as one.** A baselined row is a prompt to move the helper onto the class the next time its file is opened. The ratchet fails a helper added outside the baseline and fails a row removed without updating it; it does **not** compel a touched file to burn its rows down. Claiming otherwise would credit the guard with enforcement it does not perform.
>
> One row is permanent by decision rather than by neglect: `src/functional/util/html.mjs::html` is the tagged-template **entry point** — a module's public API that happens to sit beside the class it constructs, not a helper that escaped one. Moving it onto that class would be a regression. The guard answers *is this a function binding at module scope beside a class?* and deliberately does not answer *is it a helper that escaped, or the module's own exported API?* — that second question is review judgment at migration time, recorded in the PR that touches the file.
